guidelines.detail: refines PROC-05 (The description makes the returns work conditional on a later customer report, while the validator identifies its start event as detached. PROC-05 addresses later triggers and separate processes; this guideline clarifies that a separate process must represent its trigger in its start event.)

refines EVT-03 (The description places a confirmation action before the follow-up email. The reference models that action as a task, while the generated model uses an intermediate catch event, so this is an element-choice error rather than a missing element. EVT-03 covers catch events for waits; this guideline clarifies the modeling choice when the description instead describes performing a confirmation.)

same as LRN-014 (The description distinguishes receiving a back-order, picking in-stock items, and receiving returned items, while the label-pair records show those actions being confused. LRN-014 already gives essentially the same guidance about retaining stated activity details in labels.)

same as LRN-001 (The description establishes these activity orders, while F13 and F17 report the corresponding sequence flows absent from the generated model. This is already covered by learned guideline LRN-001.)
kept for this example only, tied to it by: performed

same as LRN-016 (The description supports the meaningful labels and details in the generated elements, while several reference labels are generic or narrower. The proposed rule is already captured by learned guideline LRN-016.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says follow-on work starts only if a later event or condition occurs after the main flow: Model the follow-on work as a conditional continuation, an event subprocess, or a separate process whose start event represents that trigger; do not leave it as an unrelated detached start-to-end chain.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says follow-on work starts only if a later event or condition occurs after the main flow

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that a participant performs an action to confirm or verify that an outcome occurred: Model the confirmation as an activity; use a catch event only when the description says the process waits for a message, signal, time, or condition.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that a participant performs an action to confirm or verify that an outcome occurred

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description explicitly names multiple operations or specifies an activity’s object or recipient: Retain those stated details in the corresponding BPMN activity label so the label does not broaden or narrow the described work.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description distinguishes activities by the object being acted on or the purpose of the action

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description lays out activities in an order, or requires several activities to finish before a later stage or process end.: Connect the activities with sequence flows that preserve the stated order; when every required activity must finish before proceeding, synchronize their paths with a parallel gateway.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that one activity must occur before another

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states an activity or outcome and identifies its action, object, actor, or recipient: label the corresponding BPMN element with concise wording that preserves those stated details and does not substitute a different action or meaning
rules_sent_back.situation: the description identifies distinct activities, events, or outcomes with their own actions or meanings

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description explicitly states that a distinct activity is performed on the output or items of an earlier activity: Model the stated activity as a separate BPMN activity and preserve the described order with sequence flows.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description explicitly states that a distinct activity is performed on the output or items of an earlier activity
